payload.meta_description: How to brief a travel advisor for your honeymoon: what to agree first, what to tell them, the questions to ask, and a brief template to copy and send.
payload.excerpt: The details that change a honeymoon shortlist, the days after the wedding that are easy to forget, the questions to ask back, and a brief template you can copy.

key_takeaways: A good honeymoon brief gives your advisor dates, a budget range and what it covers, your pace, each partner's must-haves and deal-breakers, and how the trip connects to the wedding.
Hotels you loved and disliked, with one line on why, tell an advisor more about your taste than any list of adjectives.
The Australian Passport Office recommends booking travel in the name in your passport, so book the honeymoon in the name on the passport you will carry.
Ask for every option in writing, with confirmed inclusions shown separately from requests, plus the deposit dates, the currency and the cancellation terms.
Our packages page suggests six to nine months for a honeymoon to lock in the right suite category, and Smartraveller suggests allowing at least six weeks for a passport.

faq.q: How far ahead should we brief a travel advisor for our honeymoon?
faq.a: Our packages page suggests six to nine months for a honeymoon to lock in the right suite category. Brief early enough to leave room for documents too: Smartraveller suggests allowing at least six weeks to get a passport.

faq.q: How much should we budget for a honeymoon?
faq.a: There is no single right figure. Agree a range you are both comfortable with, decide what it covers (flights, stays, experiences) and put both in the brief, so the advisor can show what it buys in each place.

A short trip taken straight after the wedding, with a longer honeymoon later. Tell your advisor it is two trips and give dates for each, so they are planned as a pair rather than one squeezed into the other.
A honeymoon shared with friends, often some of your wedding guests. It changes the brief: more rooms, possibly a group booking, and a clear note on who pays for what before any deposit is taken.
There is no single rule, and customs differ between families and cultures. If anyone is contributing, tell your advisor whose name holds the booking, who pays the deposits and in what currency.

faq.q: Is there a downside to using a travel agent?
faq.a: One is avoidable: a vague brief brings back generic options and several rounds of revisions. The other is cost clarity, so ask how the advisor is paid and whether any fee applies before any work starts.
